question: Does the target high-power difference remain among positive-production weekdays at the same hour, and is there enough overlapping temperature support for a narrower weather comparison?
input: Original 2021 Jan-Aug valid hours, fixed high label peak of four power slots >=182; retain zeros and repeated profiles; do not use derived factory-personnel or same-time power as a covariate.
primary: Summarize target by period x weekend x current production zero/positive. For weekday positive-production hours, standardize high rate across 24 exact hour cells using pooled exposure and repeat inverse profile frequency weighting. Current production is posthoc context, not an intervention.
temperature_support: For weekday positive-production hours, define a common temperature range as intersection of period-specific 5th-95th percentile intervals, without using the target. Report exposure, dates, high hours and exact-hour common cells in this range. Compute common-hour descriptive rates only if both periods have at least 10 dates and at least 12 cells each with 10 hours per period. Otherwise stop and report insufficient support.
decision: If within-context gap remains, rule out only the claim that period difference is entirely due to weekday/production composition. If it reverses, revise that claim. Temperature overlap comparison is descriptive and cannot establish weather causality.
